message:
The situation is this.  HF needs to upgrade our entire backed.  Upgraded PHP, MySQL, Nginx, Apache, NodeJS, and the OS.  It's vital because without the upgrade of the server we can't really do modern development and improvements to HF.  Our backend is out of date, so much so it's now becoming a liability.  I can't do the integrations and usage of new libraries without this.

I have a new server with excellent specs already provisioned.  I now am faced with the task of building up the new server.  The last time I did this seems like a decade ago or more.  I do have anxiety about the process but I have no choice, this must get done.  I'm choosing this week to really push through because my wife is on an 8 day vacation and this is my chance to work without family interruption.  

This is my workflow plan.

1. Install OS.
2. Install Control Panel and services.
3. Customize server for security and special needs of HF.
4. Move HF to new server (but not change DNS records).
5. Use my Hosts file to point my computer to new server as HF.
6. Begin working to update the site.
7. Once HF is functional on new server, change DNS for everyone.
8. Continue fixing and upgrading anything broken (which is going to be a lot).


Very likely we're going to lose Convo.  I just expect this.  It's not the highest priority given the overall forums is more important.  I won't give up on Convo but it's also just one feature and I'm fairly sure we can live without it for a week or more.  Fixing on-site errors (PHP, MYSQL) will take priority.  

I plan on changing how our web socket works which is notify and convo.  Fairly sure I'll be able to fix notifications quicker than Convo.  It's a simple system. Or I'll just rebuild it from scratch.  They are actually integrated and going forward I may attempt to completely separate them. Both run under NodeJS as app.js but would be better imho as notify.js and convo.js instead.  Currently the socket is on a different port.  Nginx does have a proxy forwarding for WS but as I stated, our version of Nginx is outdated and doesn't support that.  This causes some strange issues like Cloudflare blocking the port because of not passing Captcha, which doesn't ever display on web socket.  Integration of the WS to port 443 (HTTPS) will fix that ongoing issue.  

I will be using AI through much of this. It's a very useful tool for coming up with configuration files like my.cnf (MySQL Configuration) and firewall (UFW/IPtables) rules.  And then I have to consider if I'll install an Agent Assistant to go through all of HF's codebase to update to PHP8.  That's going to be very experimental for me.  

The good news, I've done this a few times, the bad news, not with NodeJS which is where I anticipate most of my struggling will come from. Some members have offered to help but I am not relying on that.  Forum member help is always unreliable and in the end, it's best that I have full control and understanding of how HF works.  If I can build it and fix it, then it's always going to be part of HF.  

I'm both confident I can do this and apprehensive about the unknown.  But this must be done and we're long past due.  I'll keep you all posted as I progress. It will be point 5 where I'll feel most energized.  That's when the real work begins.  

Thank you.

I'm getting fed up with the constant abusive DMCA notices.  It's like 3 this week now, all related to VPNs like Cyberghost. 

DMCA notices negatively effect SEO and while I counter-notice many of them it's time consuming and the general consensus is that repeated DMCA notices to a domain hurts rankings and Trust Score.

I just sent Cyberghost this email.  I will be sending these types of emails more often.

[quote]CyberGhost Legal / Compliance Team,

I am writing to formally notify you of repeated DMCA takedown notices submitted by CyberGhost that target content on our platform (hackforums.net) which is not infringing and, in many cases, not even copyrightable subject matter. These notices have included posts containing user commentary, publicly available promotions, coupon information, and links to your own website, without any copyrighted images, files, software, or redistributed material.

We have disputed multiple notices through Google, and the affected content has been restored after review. These repeated submissions have nevertheless caused measurable SEO and traffic harm due to temporary delisting and suppression. Continued submission of DMCA notices against non-copyrightable or fair-use content materially misrepresents the nature of the content and raises serious concerns of bad-faith enforcement under 17 U.S.C. §512(f). Please confirm that future enforcement actions will be reviewed for copyright eligibility before submission. If these notices continue, we will preserve all records and evaluate further legal remedies.[/quote]

Here is also a thread I posted complaining in May...
https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6298533

btw, this is the thread which got DMCA notice this morning...(an actual coupon from Cyberghost).
https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=4454481

If any of these companies bothered they could contact HF directly and ask for removal. The DMCA to Google, that pisses me off.  

Do I have a legal recourse, maybe, likely to get me anything, unlikely. Get their attention and maybe have them behave better, I hope so.

I checked and in May 2025 I did a review of HF's policies and tried to appeal the Manual Penalty on HF in Google Search Console.

We don't get listed in News and Discovery.  This has been since 2023.

Here is the contact I originally got from them.

[quote]To the owner of https://hackforums.net/:

Google periodically reviews sites to ensure that Google offers an excellent experience for our users.

Google has higher expectations and standards for content served on our Discover feed and News surfaces. Therefore, our Discover and News policies include additional behavioral and content rules that don't apply to web results and non-News surfaces.

Upon a recent review, Google identified policy violating behavior related to our Transparency or Deceptive Practices policies, which requires that publishers provide clear dates and bylines, as well as information about authors, editorial boards, ownership, primary purpose, and relationships with other publishers and entities, and non-generic contact information.

Because of the violation, your site is no longer eligible to appear on News or Discover surfaces. These actions don't affect how your site or pages appear on Search outside of News and Discover surfaces, including Search web results.

What you can do next:
1
Recommended actions
Review and update your pages to comply with the Transparency and Deceptive Practices guidelines in our News policies and Discovery policies. Simple deletion of violating content will not be considered as a reason to lift a manual action.
2
Submit a reconsideration request

Once you’ve fixed the page, updated your editorial guidelines, or if you think an error has been made, file for reconsideration. Include any details or documentation that can help us understand the changes made to your site and editorial practices with the specific reasons you think your site is no longer in violation. Reconsideration requests must be submitted within 2 weeks of receipt of this notification and we allow a maximum of 2 reconsideration requests per manual action. If you take no further action or if your reviews are unsuccessful, this manual action will remain active for 6 months, at which time you may file an additional reconsideration request.[/quote]

This is when I got rid of the Blogs thinking it was the problem.  HF is anonymous for most members, I think Google wants the Authors names and "transparency", which given our sites nature of privacy.  

Twice now I've attempted to make the adjustments and waited for the response. I just now got another denial.  Looks to me like we're not getting rid of that.  Since I removed the Blogs for this, I have enabled them again.  Not sure what the future holds for our Blog system but I don't see how it can harm HF.

Please note the Manual Penalty doesn't effect Google Search Results. It's only their News and Discovery which if pretty much the Mobile users who open things like Google News and have feeds to see new stuff.  HF is still in the search engine just fine. 

SEO, it's so much for nowadays.

Enjoy the return of the blogs. I have to find a link placement, I really didn't like the old one.   https://hackforums.net/blog.php

I just had a discussion with a member who missed the old days of bumping.  He's not the first to complain about how our Marketplace listing is by Thread Creation date.  The original change got rid of LQP bumps, friend bumps (groups were doing this), and fake accounts by sellers.  It also forced usage of Bytes for Stanley Bumps which was very efficient.  

But in good-faith after discussions with the member I'm open to seeing how reversing the change would be seen by the community and if the old bad-habits will return.  

Back then I don't believe we had any official bump policy but generally speaking the Staff told sellers not more than once in a 24 hour period and to try to add something of quality to the post and not just "bump" or some other LQ post.  For now I suppose that's once again how we'll start off.  

As always I'm happy to review policies on HF and see if adjustments improve the community experience.  

Hope you enjoy and thank you.

I've been getting a lot of comments lately about certain high-profile members controlling HF due to their monetary benefits.  Shockingly I think I have to explain a few things.  First and foremost, HF is as business. I didn't create this website as a hobby for shits and giggles.   All the websites (hundreds of them) I've built were with revenue in mind.  It didn't matter if the site made $5 a month, it was part of my network.  HF took off and in such a way it has consumed all my time and resources but it has done well enough that it's justified.  

Like any business you're always considering the bottom line.  It's a large part of the thought process when making decisions.  There is no shame in this, it's called BUSINESS.  Every business does this.  If you have a client that represents a good portion of your revenue, that customer gets priority and courtesy that a small client won't get.  This fact seems to upset people and they point it out like I should be ashamed or that it's some secret.  Catering to your higher-revenue clientele is absolutely normal.

I'm a VIP at some places in town, I get little perks like skipping lines.  I see the faces of people who might have waited 45 minutes for a table and I just walk in, flash my VIP card, and get immediate seating.  I don't feel shame, I'm a high paying customer, I get this perk offered to me by them.  And why? Because I spend an appropriate amount of money.  This is BUSINESS and basically everyone operates like this in some way.  If you don't like it, you're probably a Socialist.

Locking this because nobody needs to reply and get closed for saying something really stupid.

Thank you.

You’ve probably noticed that Hack Forums has seen a lot of change recently. Some long-time members are no longer with us, either by my decision or their own. This wasn’t something I took lightly, but sometimes in order to move forward, you have to clear a path first.

My goal is to take HF in a new direction. That means rethinking how we operate, what kind of community we want, and what kind of members we want to attract. I know that change can be uncomfortable, especially for those who have grown used to the way things were. But real progress happens when you step outside your comfort zone.

The truth is, some people were holding us back, whether they realized it or not. They wanted things to stay exactly as they were, and they weren’t open to new ideas. I want HF to be more than just a place to hang out and chat. I want members who have a vision, who want to build, who bring something new to the table.

Losing active members isn’t easy, and I know it has an effect on the community. Some people are upset, and I get that. But you can’t remove toxic influences without also upsetting a few of their friends. That’s just how it works. I stand by my decision, because I believe it’s necessary for the next phase of HF.

If you’re still here, it means you’re open to where HF could go. I encourage you to be part of this shift. Bring your ideas, your skills, and your passion. Let’s see if we can make HF into something better. Maybe it won’t work, but I’d rather try and fail than not try at all.

I'm locking this because I just want to express myself more than I need replies and feedback.  

Thanks for sticking with us through the changes.  Expect great things.

message:
Currently HF has a function to deal with Race Conditions. If you don't know that that is...

[aiq]A PHP race condition occurs when multiple processes or requests attempt to access and modify shared resources (e.g., a database, file, or session) simultaneously, leading to unpredictable or incorrect outcomes. For example, if two requests try to update a user’s point balance in a MyBB forum at the same time, one update might overwrite the other, causing data inconsistency, such as double-spending points.

In PHP, race conditions often arise in web applications due to concurrent HTTP requests, especially in systems without proper synchronization. They can be mitigated using techniques like database transactions, row locking (e.g., `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), or time-based checks, as seen in your `form_post_check` function, which prevents rapid submissions to avoid conflicts in functions like `processSigPurchase`.[/aiq]

Basically we want to make sure that Bytes can't get exploited but other things too have to be checked.  

I'm altering the function because it's been buggy.  Added some debugging logs as well.  

What I'm asking is for members to help me test the Race Conditions on HF and offering a 1000 Bytes Bounty if you can find them in the Bytes system.

You can also test other areas but I will only grant 250 Bytes bounty if a race condition is found.

Please if you find one, DO NOT POST.  Instead please send me a PM with the details.  I'll need to know the page and action you're doing at least. 

Thank you.

So this morning got up, had my coffee, got to work.  After dealing with contacts (email, convo, pms) I looked around the forum made some posts.  Eventually after about 2 hours I took a look at the Roadmap seeing what I can fit in with the short time I have today (2-3 hours).

This is where it gets fun.

I see in the Roadmap to build a page on Hackforums.com for SEO.  Should be easy enough, likely use AI to do the heavy work.  To do this I have to host the page.  Decided to use one of my many VPS's I have.  Took me a few to check the configuration, login, and whatnot.  I see the panel on this server very old, could use a replacement.  Server has just one basic job and I can probably remove it but meh.  I'll use it.  Looked at a couple panels quick.  Then I noticed one of the 3 domains on this VPS didn't work. Go check configs, view DNS....hmm...odd.   Then I see that I have a database on this server using a webhook from the mail service I use, it logs all the errors. I see it's a fairly large database now. I run some checks on it and see stuff I don't like.  Now I have to go check HF code see what's up.  What's suppose to happen is the VPS logs errors, then tells HF about it, then on HF I remove that members subscription to either the thread or the forum subscription. This way someone shouldn't continue to get email  sent wasting my resources with bounced un-deliverable emails.  Except it doesn't appear to be working as I see from the logs some members have as many as 2000+ errors.  Now I have to deal with this. I do about an hour of checking all the code, everything looks fine. I do have some debugging options in the code which I enabled but I have to wait for bounces to see results.   Now my 2-3 hours is about up.  I quickly go setup the DNS for HackForums.com, will take time to propagate.  In the meantime I now have to double-check my email error logging situation which will be more work and I've barely started with the HF.com.  

So that's how half a day of work goes very often.  I end up not accomplishing what I set out to do and I end up with something new on my list.  

This thread is so maybe I can get some understanding  (not sympathy) that this isn't easy and getting major projects done can be difficult.  

Thanks for reading.

message:
This is the moment I'm asking for some feedback on the new theme changes.

Spent most of the day tweaking little things.  You  might need to F5+CTRL in your browser to refresh the cache.  


Instructions to Refresh Cache:
[sp]
[aiq]Refreshing (clearing) your browser cache on a mobile device depends on **which browser and platform** you use. Here are instructions for the most common scenarios:

---

## **Android**

### **Chrome**

1. Open Chrome.
2. Tap the three dots (⋮) in the top-right corner.
3. Tap **History** > **Clear browsing data…**
4. Select **Cached images and files** (you can uncheck others if you only want cache).
5. Tap **Clear data**.

### **Samsung Internet**

1. Tap the three lines (≡) > **Settings** > **Privacy** > **Delete browsing data**.
2. Select **Cache** (and anything else you want).
3. Tap **Delete data**.

### **Firefox**

1. Tap the three dots (⋮) > **Settings** > **Delete browsing data**.
2. Select **Cache**.
3. Tap **Delete browsing data**.

---

## **iPhone / iPad**

### **Safari**

1. Go to **Settings** app (not Safari itself).
2. Scroll down, tap **Safari**.
3. Tap **Clear History and Website Data**.

   * *Warning:* This will log you out of websites, not just clear cache.

### **Chrome**

1. Open Chrome.
2. Tap the three dots (•••) at the bottom or top right.
3. Tap **History** > **Clear Browsing Data**.
4. Select **Cached Images and Files**.
5. Tap **Clear Browsing Data**.

### **Firefox**

1. Tap the three horizontal lines (≡) > **Settings**.
2. Tap **Data Management**.
3. Toggle **Cache**.
4. Tap **Clear Private Data**.

---

## **Hard Refresh (without clearing all cache)**

Most mobile browsers **do not support a true "hard refresh"** (like Ctrl+F5 on desktop). However, you can:

* **Reload the page multiple times**.
* **Close the tab, reopen, and reload**.
* **Use “Clear Cache”** as above for a guaranteed result.

[/aiq][/sp]

I wouldn't say I'm completely done with changes.  Will adjust according to feedback or little things I see need improving.  Me personally, I love it 100%.  But maybe you don't?   Or maybe you found a bug with display that needs to get fixed.  In any case this is your moment to make a response.

Meh, just some sharing and thoughts.  Been up since 6am and typing like a madman.  Gonna see how much further I can push today before my brain says "NO MORE".

message:
Back in February I got a $20 Account Recovery Fee for the member @Lrrr@.  This was the inital message...

[quote]Forgot my password, inactive for a while. Miss this forum so much...I would like to get back....I used to have 2fa everywhere so once my phone got broken I cant login even to my email....big loss. Would like my account back with new email and password.[/quote]

After looking at the account I saw he's not been online for almost 2 years.  Almost immediately I got email contacts asking about the Recovery.  The problem was that my checks on the account showed no matching IP's to the person attempting to recover. They didn't know the account email nor have any other information linking the account.  And Lrrr is a very reputable account, even more reason for me to be very diligent.  

I had probably 20 emails back and forth with this person attempting to recover. On the actual account email I sent a contact hoping to get a response, nothing.  The account thief even went so far as to contact other members to "vouch" for them.  Two members both told me it was suspicious and they either didn't know Lrrr that well or that they believed this was an account thief.  

A lot of time was wasted on this and eventually the person went away, I told them point blank I can't recover the account.  I then proceeded to ban the account out of caution.  

Today I got a reply and contact from the actual Lrrr who was grateful I was diligent and they hadn't checked their account email in a while.  

So a few things to learn from this.

1. The $20 Recovery Fee is there for a reason.   It dissuades account thieves from attempts.  It covers the time I might have to put into confirming the account owner.
2. Fighting Bots crawling HF is important because one of the bot'd pages is member profiles.  My guess is they're looking for a few things but one is definitely prominent accounts that might have Credibility but maybe haven't logged in for a while.
3. Be diligent about protecting your account by ensuring you have 2FA enabled and definitely backup the Secret Key.
4. I ain't no sucker falling for the bullshit.

Also,  I think another account was attempted to get stolen/recovered to a thief a few weeks later.  

Anyways, thought this was an interesting story to share.  Had mentioned it in Convo so maybe some rumors floating around.  

Enjoy your day.

message:
In case you haven’t heard — on the afternoon of April 1st, my BTC and LTC Electrum wallets were drained. Looks like someone got their April Fool’s joke at my expense.

I’m still in the process of setting up an entirely new system, and while some parts take time (like transferring massive files), I’m able to pop in and make some posts or join Convo. However, I’m not fully operational yet — most of my tools aren't set up, so real work is still on hold.

I believe the Electrum wallets were compromised because the wallet seeds were exposed. I didn’t have passwords on those wallet files. Yeah, I know — lazy. But these were active daily wallets with funds constantly flowing in and out, and for the sake of speed and convenience, I left them unprotected. That’s likely how the attacker got the keys.

Thankfully, my Exodus wallet was password-protected and untouched. I also keep serious funds in cold storage, which wasn’t affected.

I suspect the initial breach came through Chrome and one of my web3 wallets. That afternoon, I noticed weird behavior — Chrome kept redirecting to a MetaMask-related site, probably trying to trick me into entering a password. That was a big red flag.

The total loss was about $700 in BTC and LTC, plus another $1,000 I had to drop on a new PC — though I was probably due for a new one this year anyway.

Going forward, I’m shifting to a more secure setup using virtual machines (via VirtualBox). I’ve tinkered with VMs before but never used them as a production setup. The plan now is to isolate all crypto activity within a dedicated, locked-down environment and keep development work in a separate one. It’ll complicate things a bit, but the added security is worth the trade-off.

I can’t say for sure if it was a RAT or just malware with a wallet-draining payload. Either way, that old system is done. I backed up and double-scanned all files with multiple antivirus tools. I believe I acted quickly enough to limit the damage — was cautious with the screen and clipboard, and took the computer offline immediately. I've since been working from my laptop.

I don’t believe HF was compromised — there’s no evidence to suggest that — but as always, there’s no 100% guarantee. While my old system stored backups and access credentials, those were inside encrypted, password-protected files and folders. I’ve seen nothing to suggest this was more than a typical wallet drainer looking for easy pickings. My guess? I’m just one of thousands randomly infected.

Still, the “just in case” factor looms large, so once I have my new setup fully functional, I’ll begin rotating credentials across the board. Rebuilding a work environment I’ve curated over the past 12 years takes time — especially now that I’m moving into a Linux-based VM setup, which adds its own learning curve.

But so far, so good.

Thank you.

Some recent events are now forcing me to officially implement some policy changes.

This was previous policy:  https://hackforums.net/misc.php?action=help&hid=35
7. Refusing to use the HF Contract system with a member you want to deal with.

Updated:
7. Anyone refusing to use HF Contracts will be closed.
8. Anyone refusing to use a Middle-man in HF Contracts will be closed.   MM has to be paid by the party requesting it.
9. All off-site deals must still use an HF Contract, if not, you will be closed.  
10. If a pattern of avoiding Contracts is apparent, you will be closed.

Basically it's time to go back to previous policy about proactively encouraging on-site deals and the use of HF Contracts.  Why?  Because avoiding Contracts is exactly how scammers get victims.  I nearly never hear complaints about deals when an HF Contract is used and with the Contract it's more clear about who is in the wrong on the deal.  While I know many feel the Contract system is just an additional step that's an annoyance, I have to weigh the cost of scams to the reputation of the site.  

Recently had a contact about someone rather upset and accusing a handful of members of being involved in a scammer ring.  I'm accused of helping them of course if I do nothing short of closing their accounts.  But how can I justify that under policy based on some random member making a vocal complaint?   This is why we have policies, they aren't just guidelines for members, they are guidelines for myself and Staff too.  Without policy this place would be chaos.  I don't want scammers on the site. I don't want members being scammed.  Scams though are always a two-way street, the scammer and the victim.  I don't understand why HF gets the blame of an off-site scam but we do.  They don't contact the admins of Discord or Telegram, they contact me.  

Another issue is false accusations.  This would not be the first time that one or more members have a vendetta and use the scammer accusation attempting to get their account closed.  That's why I need an HF Contract.  I have no proof that two parties were in a deal without them.  And current policy very clear that we won't get involved in Deal Disputes without a Valid Active HF Contract.  

If you think my policies are overly harsh keep in mind we literally have threat-actors actively finding victims on HF and I'm pretty sure BKRandy and Blunt are on the site right now under reputable accounts just waiting for a Big Score.  I'm trying to protect all members. 

Stop being pricks and use HF Contracts if you're a buyer and sellers, if you don't accept a Contract, you will be CLOSED.  

Thank you.

message:
Last night (previous 12 hours or so) our tunnel appears to have gone offline.  Well technically our connection to the tunnel went offline.  Sometimes that happens. When it does some features on the site won't work. Those include Country Lock, IP checking, Avatar Uploads, and Invoices (BTCpay server).  

So if you did experience some odd behavior from HF the past 12 hours, that's almost surely the reason.

What is a tunnel?  It's a SSH connection to another server to move traffic from HF origin server to outside connections.

Why does HF run a tunnel?  It hides our actual IP to prevent direct DDoS attacks.  Anytime the HF server has to do an outside server https call it uses the tunnel.  For example external API's.  This way even if say an API we use has an employee that wants to know HF's IP from the logs, they don't have it.  

Why did it go offline?  Could be anything, likely some datacenter network disruption that broke the connection.  

Oh and takes me 10 seconds to enable the connection again.  It goes offline maybe once a year. It's very rare.

It was reported to me a bug that Bytes were actually not being deducted when bumping.  It probably worked with the API but definitely was not deducting from the thread bump.  Seems that there is a conflict in the query flow causing this.  The fix was to make sure the Bytes are deducted in the shutdown sequence.  

You can read more about Shutdown here:  https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.register-shutdown-function.php

MyBB actually has a shutdown function in their query class $db->shutdown_query() which is what I used to fix this.  

Anyways, after spending a couple hours on the frustrating bug I have decided to lower Bump costs.

Regular/L33t 150->100
Ub3r 100->75
Vendors 50 (no change)

Also, my alteration could potentially cause side-effects in other functions where Bytes are added/subtracted. If by chance you see any odd behavior related to that please report it to me.  Make sure the Bytes system is working properly please.

Enjoy and thanks.

Within 24 hours I get wind that he scammed $78k in a months long Social Engineering scam.   Now his need to be deleted made sense and I'm rather angry about it.  Not that I could ever help the victim recover and my only recourse was to close Dyne/Snyke anyways.  Realistically my only true power on the site.  

Dyne is a masterful Social Engineer.  I suspect multiple accounts are easily achieved for him. Including accounts which build up reputation and site notoriety.  Here is why I'm making this thread, I suspect that @Scrubspoof@ is either in on the scam or is actually Dyne as well.  Why do I think this, gut instinct.  Yeah, I know that's technically not the best route to go when it comes to taking action on an account but with a $78k scam I'm too pissed off to really give a fuck.  If I suspected an HF group was involved it would have already been deleted.  For now I have banned Scrubspoof while I investigate.  

To add to the story, some weeks ago Scrubspoof paid me as well to open a new account, but I have to admit, I was a bit confused because I thought it was Dyne. Scrubspoof of course swears he wasn't involved in the scam nor is he Dyne.  Seems to me some member input might clarify what I should do.  I don't feel comfortable closing him if he's not Dyne but I also don't feel after this scam he should be trusted at all.

message:
So the past 24 hours we've been under a massive DDoS.  The good news, it's not effecting us at all.  It's being blackholed.  However, I'm starting to believe that this is a government sanctioned attack.  Bear with me as I explain.


Here is the over 1b hits...
[img]https://i.imgur.com/g0d3p3V.png[/img]


These are the 3 datacenters involved.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/SFrO8Yl.png[/img]

https://bgp.he.net/AS3320
https://lg.telekom.com  AS3320 Deutsche Telekom AG

https://bgp.he.net/AS8220
https://www.colt.net  Colt Technologies

https://bgp.he.net/AS1273 Vodafone Group UK

All 3 seem to be coming from EU based cell providers, one is UK, one is German, and not sure yet about Colt.  Normally DDoS attacks are all over the map but not this one, it's as if the attacks are intended from the inside of the datacenters.  In other words...coordinated.  You might ask, well why would they do that?  Because of these attacks I'm forced to block the entire ASN, which means a TON of people in UK and Germany can't access HF without a VPN.  My guess is that's the intent.

Note how evenly distributed the attack is from each datacenter?  How is that possible unless it's coordinated by the datacenters themselves?  

Both UK and Germany continue to have totalitarian laws on free speech that does include topics on hacking. We all know the NCA has an account here and my guess is that German officials do as well.  Maybe they think I'll block these countries so the attack stops?  

I'm just puzzled why anyone would carry on attack for so long that's not even slowing HF down.  Who would waste such resources in a vain attempt? What would be the purpose otherwise?  

What do you think?  Am I just crazy paranoid or am I onto something?  Do you think government agencies would do this? Yes, I am speculating but hey, it's all fun.

So how do I combat that?  

Starting shortly I will making an adjustment to the PM system.  Non-upgraded members will be unable to PM each other.  That's going to actually protect new members from being targeted for these off-site scams which are almost always from other non-upgraded members.

Feel free to leave some feedback.  I hope to implement this change within a week but possibly a lot sooner.

message:
When I am mobile I have continually noticed that the socket doesn't work for me.  I've had a couple members state they have the issue. This thread is to get feedback and discuss the issue.

Anyone else that has experienced the problem of Convo and Notify not working while mobile please chime-in. 

Issue is that you'll see that you have notifications but when you click it, it's empty, not loading any data.  With Convo you can see the listings of your Convo's but when you go into group convo or a private convo data doesn't load.  That's the symptom.  The cause, it's because of Cloudflare protections.  Even though I have bypass for the socket it doesn't seem to work correctly.  Cloudflare wants to give you a CAPTCHA but since it's a websocket you never see it, so it doesn't get solved, so the socket doesn't work for you. Happens to me at the oddest moments from normal IPs without a VPN.

I have for myself fixed this by installing Cloudflare Warp and enabling just the DNS part.  Seems to work mostly but not all the time. So a change in IP or connection type is how you get past the Cloudflare Captcha attempt which then allows the socket to load.  This is a shitty fix obviously and long-term not how I'll be dealing with it.

Unsure if recently this is happening to more and more members but I've noticed that we're getting less people in Convo. I'm wondering if this is possibly why.   

What is the fix you may be asking yourself?  Well right now our websocket is on a different port.  When you connect to HF you're 443 (NGINX HTTPS) and 2096 (websocket).  Nginx does do websocket proxy.

https://www.nginx.com/blog/websocket-nginx/  

Unfortunately it requires upgrading our backend first.  I can't yet implement the fix until we're moved to the new server.   Attempting to upgrade our current server is more likely going to break things more than fix them.   But overall it's good news there is a way to resolve the problem permanently.  Once we proxy to the port from 443/80 then when you past Cloudflare Captcha on the site, it should also work for the socket.   That's the theory anyways.

I'm sharing to keep you updated but I really want to know how many other members are experiencing socket issues.  Surely can't just be a few of us.  I think it's more widespread and people are likely just frustrated.  

Thanks.

message:
As for today I have been provisioned a new dedicated server. The intent is to move HF onto this server within 3-6 months.  The reason for the long timeframe is because HF currently runs on old technology and our entire backend has to be updated. For example we're on a 7.x PHP which is past EOL and I know for a fact that HF will break updating to 8.3 (latest PHP).  Also our NodeJS is outdated and my guess is that an update will break some of those components (convo and socket).  

I will need months to setup the server and it's going to be a huge workload which I plan to spread out until I am comfortable that a move will appear seamless to members.

Some of the steps I am taking.

1.  Setup server security.
2.  Install Control Panel (makes my life easier)
3.  Setup a dummy test domain.
4.  Backup HF and move to test domain.
5.  Fix all the broken parts.
6.  Switch the test domain for HF domain and go live.

Seems simple enough when laid out like that but trust me, lots and lots of work.  That's just a breakdown but there are a hundreds of little details in each of those.  The biggest challenge will actually be the NodeJS stuff for me since JS is not a language I'm comfortable with.  I am hoping some AI assistance along with diligence will get me through it.  

Overall this is very good news for HF. Once we are updated there are options for upgrading features on HF at my disposal. Currently I can't do too much because all the libraries and packages won't work on our older setup.  Example is AI integrations.  

I look forward to the work and completion.  I hope you do too.  This thread is basically just an official announcement.  

Thank you.

Someone forwarded to me logs with some HF member accounts.  The list was over 5000 entries.  Of those checked against the HF DB it appears around 650 regular members, 20 L33t, and about 9 Ub3r accounts.  

After testing some of the passwords in the logs did work to login to HF.  This means they used the same password on whatever site the logs were from.  That is a bad security practice.  

To prevent potential scams and stolen accounts,  I have closed all the non-upgraded accounts.  All the L33t and Ub3r accounts have their PW's changed and they will need to perform a PW Reset.  

HF servers and site is in no way compromised.  This is just foolish people reusing their PWs.  Don't do that.

Thank you.
subject: Account Breaches

message:
It's becoming an issue that HF is actually being blocked by security software.  Let's say you go to Starbucks, enable their Wifi, then you find out you get a DNS error. That's not because HF is blocking you or Starbucks, it's because Starbucks has security software so you're not viewing malicious sites or maybe porn.  This means from many public Wifi areas you might not be able to use HF unless you use your own VPN or Proxy.  

What I am going to do starting today is set all my ASN blocks to be Challenges instead.  This means you'll get some page that will tell you to wait a moment while it sees if you're human before HF loads.  

The Country Blocks are still in place.  Those are blocked for even better reasons and will remain so.

Unfortunately I anticipate that this experiment in policy won't last long. That we'll have more problems with scammers, spammers, and DDoS attacks.  So I definitely can't promise this will remain policy indefinitely.  But for now, if you have a VPN or proxy, give it a try and see if HF loads.

The good news is that Cloudflare does have some new DDoS protection management so it's also possible that those will be more effective and thus the ASN blocks may not be needed.  I will be monitoring this closely.

Thank you.

Uber 100 Bytes
Everyone Else = 150 Bytes

Please note that after you Bump with Stanley in the thread it will appear that the thread creation date has not changed, that's because it is displaying the date from the posts table. Really our $18 for 6 months is only $3 a month.  I've always considered HF's pricing levels incredibly cheap.  I never wanted our upgrades to be pricey, but maybe I'll change that and go the route of earning upgrades through activity and/or a pricier model.

message:
So it appears that Convo has an issue with upload size limits.  I just banged out 2 hours trying to figure it out.  

Issue seems to be that when you upload a file over 1mb the socket disconnects you.  I do not know why. It's seemingly unrelated to Nginx or Apache as I was able to upload a 3mb txt file just fine through MyBB.  

I'm looking through all the nodejs code and I don't see where a 1mb limit does this nor can I find any evidence of a default restriction causing the problem. There is nothing in logs either.  

I'm going to continue working on this but for now I have updated the convo js so that it simply provides you an error on the 1mb instead of disconnecting your socket.  

The current method of uploading and displaying the images is we base64 encode them.  It's actually a good way to do it for security.  We don't technically store files on HF so if you uploaded a payload it's not gonna do anything.

Members can CTRL+F5 this file to get the latest version with the 1mb limit. Or just stay with the one you have and it will basically just socket disconnect you on files between 1mb and 2mb.

https://hackforums.net/jscripts/convo_223.js

Meh.  I hope I can get this resolved within a reasonable time frame. The goal is to fix it so the limit is maybe 3mb so that camera images actually work to upload.

Thank you.

Scroll to the bottom of any page and you should see the 3 little bars.  The left is Black, the middle is the default grey (#282828) and the right one is the lightest option (#343434).  If you choose black or lightest then it sets a cookie.  By choosing default (in the middle) no cookie is set or any JS executed because it's the sites default BG for the theme.  

This is some simple JS I whipped up to do this.  Since everyone was divided on the best background I have chosen to go this route. I think it should make many of you happy.  

Please note that since this does work on a cookie, if you go into your cookie and alter it for a different hex code like #FF00FF then that will be the background. It should make [mention=1306528] pretty happy as it will be super easy to add something like this to HFX.

message:
Currently HF doesn't send marketing emails.  Basically in 15 years I believe I have only sent an email blast out 3 times and once was to alert of a security breach.  All the emails sent from HF are transactional for things like registration, notifications of PMs, member opt-in subscriptions (threads and such) and Password Resets.  

I'm curious to get feedback on how HF members would feel if I did have an official newsletter that went out either monthly or weekly.  I may even work with the HF Writers and HF News group to create a good format and provide content.  

Would you consider this spammy or actually read the emails?  

My fear is that members would too often "Unsubscribe" from all HF emails which even prevents them from getting PW resets and they have to subscribe again. Often I have to walk them through it but if they just read they'd see how to fix it themselves.  I am also not the biggest fan of email marketing. 

What's your view on some of this?

Intent for example might include some sponsored content, important new threads, contest info, and whatever else I can find appropriate.

We inflated from 11m to 16m in the past 30 days. Last I looked a year ago I think we were near 8m.  So this was an alarming jump.

Each of those members used the exploit.  Likely sharing it in their groups Discord.  

The exploit was simple enough and 100% our fault.  We had HUM bounties set in a calculation based partially off how much the HUM was fed during its life.  When you kill the HUM you get the bounty. Easy enough. Except that more recently we added a resurrection spell.  Unfortunately we didn't reset that calculation data.  So members were exploiting this by building up their HUMs, killing them, resurrecting them, and killing them again.  Sometimes they would do this 3-4 times to the same HUM.  That's collusion and not the intent of the bounty.  

Thus I have reset everyone involved to 10 Bytes.  Also anyone who had Bytes in the crypto game, those are gone too.

The scope of the HUM exploit led to at least an extra 5m Bytes. I am still investigating and tracking down all the logs for each of those involved. 

I know that those who used the exploit likely sold off some of the Bytes. So it would be unfair of me to delete those.  You are likely safe if that was the case.  

The biggest disappointment is that a lot of high profile members were involved and no one came forward about it.  I did ban most people involved but I am going to lift their bans.  I'm sure from their perspective they just played the game but they knew what they were doing. 

A younger me probably would have reset all the bytes.  I literally did that years ago. So don't complain about the action taken.  It's the fairest thing I can do.

If someone has some additional knowledge about this or maybe I missed some bytes somewhere I need to destroy please PM me asap.

Thank you.

message:
Well this is going to be the truth about what happened the past 72 hours even though it's going to be a bit embarrassing.  

HF gets attacks, a lot of them, all the time.  I have a lot of automated security and get alerts if I'm away from my computer and HF goes offline.

When I take vacations I do not announce it for security reasons.  Well, it just so happened a reasonable sized attack hit HF just as I was driving to California for the weekend to spend with family and friends.  It's a 5 hour drive and I sat in agony the whole time as HF loaded slowly and I tried to communicate some actions to Xerotic. I was not driving btw. 

I arrived in California Thursday afternoon around 3pm but immediately I have something planned till about 6pm.  I know HF is loading slowly and the web socket isn't working and SSL Handshake errors are all over the place.  Unfortunately I didn't have availability to deal with it.  

Note that Xerotic is not a system administrator and his access to HF servers is limited.  He does not have root access nor the skillset (yet) to manage the server.  It's something I hope to guide him more with our test servers before giving him access to the HF servers.

About 6pm hits and I'm back at my hotel room and I whip open my laptop to take a look.  I'd say that I'm a DDOS mitigation specialist because that's one of my main tasks running HF and I've been doing it for 14 years.  

This is where it gets embarassing for me.  I normally don't need to use my laptop on trips.  I always bring it but rarely have needed it. My automated  DDOS protection has been fairly strong. But I always carry with me my credentials for access.  When I finally did begin working with the laptop I was having trouble logging into the server as root.  Root access is very much required to deal with a DDOS attack.  I had only about 2 hours Thursday night before our dinner plans.  I was not able to login as root.  

Then on Friday morning I woke up extra early to get it sorted out.  I got very close but again, did not gain root access in the two hour window I had before my scheduled events.  It was really frustrating for me.  I was kicking myself for not 100% confirming my access and setting up the laptop before leaving for vacation.  I'm certain given enough time I'd have gotten into the server but it was unfair to my family and friends to also ruin their plans.  

By Friday afternoon I made the decision to turn HF off for the weekend until I returned Sunday to properly deal with the issue.  

It took me about 15 minutes to normalize HF.  Took about 10 minutes more for attacks to resume and even less time for me to stop the attack.  One person is claiming responsibility and trying to blackmail me for 1 BTC.  Another person on social media claims HF has a RAT on the server.  I'm sure other rumors were spread during the downtime.

1. No RAT on the server. That's ridiculous because you don't install RAT's into a LINUX server.  You install a SHELL.

2. Not gonna ever pay any ransom.

3. Attack was shit and easily stopped once I was in the server.  

4. I don't care about the identity of the attacker nor about their motivation.  I'm only ever concerned about keeping HF online.

5. HF is secure.  Our server is not compromised. All data is safe and also backups exist off-server.

I assume the attacker will continue attacking.  I don't really care.  I'll figure it out and adjust and we'll continue business as usual.  The ONLY reason we were effected was because I was on vacation.  DDOS attacks are very normal part of my day.  

On Friday I had Xerotic extend all HF paid advertising (Banners, Stickies, Sales Tags, and Featured Forum) for 3 days.  So anyone with advertising should not be upset over lost time.  

Meh, back to business as usual. I certainly want to apologize to everyone for being an idiot and locking myself out of server.  Really noobish thing to do. It won't happen again.

Thank you.
subject: HF Downtime Nov 2020

message:
Introducing the game, "/Dev/Null:Ports".


[sp=Image Guide][img]https://i.imgur.com/RDFs6KB.png[/img][/sp]

[sp=Game Rules]/Dev/Null : Ports

Object of the Game:  To find your opponents CPU before they find yours.

Ports: Currently there are 9 ports to choose from.  If the port is green, it's never been pinged, if it's yellow then it was previously pinged, if it's black then that's a /dev/null port and does not contain your opponents CPU.  If a port is glowing red that's because it's the last port to be pinged so you won't lose your place in the game.

Attacks:  There are 4 attack types.  SQLi, Virus, XSS, and the DDOS.  Each has a power ranking of 1-5 (5 is highest) which is viewable as dots as part of their respective buttons.  

Defenses: There are 3 defenses usable. They are WAF (Web Application Firewall), VPN (Virtual Private Network) and AV (Anti-Virus).  The defenses each have a power ranking from 1 to 5, 5 being the best defense.  Please note the AV defense is always available but has a low success rate, you must roll a 6.

Cooldowns:  An attack or defense once used goes into a cooldown mode which makes the item unusable for that many turns.  

Cooldown Resets:  You have the opportunity to reset cooldowns of either your attack or your defense depending on which moment you choose to allow your opponent to see a /dev/null port.  If during the initial Ping phase you choose /Dev/Null option then all your attack cooldowns reset.  If during your defense move option you choose the /Dev/Null option then all defense cooldowns reset.  

Rolls:  All success rates of attacks and defenses are down randomly with a dice roll.  The success rate depends on the power of the item being used.  A roll of 6 is always a success while a roll of 1 is always a fail.  An example; the Virus is an attack power 4.  You will need to roll a 3, 4, 5, or 6 for your attack to succeed.  Your opponent might choose their VPN as a defense and they will need a 4, 5, or 6 to successfully defend.

To Start:  Click "Find Match", this will connect you to another opponent who is in the queue and also clicked the Find Match button.

Turn Example:

1. Xerotic (player 1) goes first.  He chooses port 7 to ping. 
2. Omniscient (player 2) sees that port 7 is being pinged and must choose to either Deny the Ping or to open it with /Dev/Null.  In his Local tab he can see where his CPU is located and it's port 9 so currently he is safe but decides strategically to Deny the Ping forcing an attack instead.
3. Xerotic chooses an attack and decides to use SQLi, he rolls a 3 which is a success.
4. Omniscient now sees there was a successful SQLi attack and must decide either to use a defense option (WAF,VPN, AV) or expose the port (/Dev/Null) thus saving his resources and resetting his defense cooldowns.  He decides to defend with a VPN, he rolls a 2 and fails the defense. The port is exposed but it is not his CPU.
5. Turn over, Xerotic's cooldowns all go down by one.

The above example is just a first move example and as the game goes on until one of the players CPU is found inside one of the ports.  The player who first finds the opponents CPU wins the game.

Stategy:  Early on with no cooldowns players will want to drain defense resources of their opponents but must use their own attack resources.  You hope your opponent doesn't Ping the Port of the CPU early in the game but even if they do it might not guarantee they beat you.  Clever attacking and defending with the timing of cooldown resets with the /Dev/Null option is crucial.  Luck is involved in every dice roll related move. Defending hard a port which is not your CPU could throw off your opponent into believing it's the CPU they found and thus they waste resources hitting hard a port that eventually can turn out to be /dev/null. 

Matches last between 3 and 15 minutes normally.  When the game ends, no matter the victor, feel free to start a new match.[/sp]

Play [url=https://hackforums.net/devnullports.php]/Dev/Null:Ports[/url] now!

Part of the benefit of Xerotic moving to Vegas is that we can work in-person which for brainstorming can be more productive.  We been talking about how to implement a form of PvP here on HF.  Before yesterday we didn't have much luck beyond some simple ideas of what we wanted but not really clicking on the direction to get started.  A PvP is really high on my priority list.

My criteria for a PvP game is simple enough.  It has to be played in 2-5 minutes most of the time.  It has to be an intuitive and simple game.  It has to be mobile compatible.  It has to be as original and hacker-ish as possible.  It needs a random factor like dice but also some skill and strategy.

Yesterday I told Xerotic to head over to my house.  And under the above criteria we started to outline a concept.  Within a couple hours we had a basis for a game.  We then proceeded to play the game with pen, paper, casino chips (used as markers) and dice.  Over the next couple hours we made adjustments as we played the game.  It was actually very exciting because almost immediately we both knew we were onto something.  We felt we had a beta version of the game ready.  Then we asked Steve to come over because we wanted to see how someone else would view the game and we wanted more feedback.  

The three of us were now taking turns playing the game one on one against each other.  And it was fantastic. Steve felt the same way we did that the game we created was unique and fun.  Games took anywhere from 3 minutes up to 20 minutes but we knew that coded into the browser would make game play a bit faster.  

Xerotic is on it right now coding away the game logic.  The game is simple enough we believe we can have a live beta on HF within a week.  Sorry but at this time we will not go into details about how the game is played.  I did want to create this thread so that members can anticipate something great coming to HF shortly.  The intent of the game is PvP with the ability of Bytes betting.  The beta will likely be a standalone page without the betting aspects but we will work quickly to integrate it into the Hack Game and do Bytes betting. 

Everyone is going to love what's coming.  My excitement level is beyond explanation.  This is the big thing HF needs for 2020. 

Thanks for reading.

message:
We had a bit of a bug with Sportsbook since implementing soccer.  Odds were given in some matches where both sides were underdogs.  Example would be Team A is +110 and Team B is +120.  In such a match you could bet both sides an equal amount.  You'd win either way and that's because a TIE in the match would refund your wager.

And that's the bug, in a soccer match if both sides are underdogs it's suppose to be a 3-way bet with win,loss,and tie odds.  Upon a tie you'd lose your wager and not be refunded as a bet draw.  

We ran some output and a couple hundred thousand bytes were created under this bug by those who knowingly exploited it.  I suppose I can't fault anyone for doing so but I also can't allow the Bytes created by this to exist.  As such we have removed most TIE wager bets for soccer matches.

About 20 members were effected but I suppose a thread is bound to come up by one of them so this explains it to everyone involved.

What we did was take those who waged at least 1000 bytes into these bets and got a tie.  We reduced their Bytes by the appropriate amount.  Some were negative or zero and in such cases we simply set the Bytes to 1000.  Others only lost a small fraction of their Bytes.

Going forward this bug is fixed by ensuring a tie in soccer matches is NOT refunded.  We will add some disclaimers on the page explaining that.

I hope this explains the situation to those involved.  Any questions?
